sources.version: Conservation Science and Practice 5(4), e12916; version of record first published 2023-03-23
sources.locator: Methods §3.1 Field data collection; Results §§4.1–4.3 and Tables 1–2; Discussion §5
sources.license: Creative Commons Attribution License (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article open-access copyright notice
sources.scope: Nest-survey and population-estimation study for orangutans identified as Pongo pygmaeus pygmaeus in forest transects within and around Danau Sentarum National Park, West Kalimantan. Only paraphrased text results are used.
sources.licenseAppliesTo: Article text under the item-level CC BY 4.0 notice; separately credited third-party material is excluded.
sources.attribution: Yuliani EL, Bakara DO, Ilyas M, Russon AE, Salim A, Sammy J, Sunderland-Groves JL, Sunderland TCH (2023). Conservation Science and Practice 5(4):e12916. https://doi.org/10.1111/csp2.12916. Claims paraphrased.

gaps: No morphology evidence was assessed in this batch.
Reproduction, development, lifespan and other life-history traits have not been assessed.

claims.text: Using an updated mean nest-decay rate of 288.3 days, the study estimated about 202 orangutans within Danau Sentarum National Park (95% CI 75.67–541.79) and about 71 outside it (95% CI 20.76–244.63); these are local model-based estimates, not direct counts.
claims.locator: Results §4.3, population estimates and Table 2; Discussion §5
claims.placeTimeScope: Ten survey locations in and around Danau Sentarum National Park, Kapuas Hulu, West Kalimantan; transect surveys were conducted in 2010–2014, with nest-decay calibration observations spanning 2010–2011. Estimates are model-derived for the sampled landscape.
claims.lifeStatus: Free-ranging orangutans detected through nests in wild and logged forest transects; no captive or domesticated animals are included.

gaps: The estimate is local and method-dependent, has wide uncertainty, and does not constitute a species-wide population estimate or complete ecological account.
No phylogenetic or evolutionary evidence was assessed.
The study's local survey sites do not provide a complete current or historical species range inventory.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No formal Red List, legal status or range-wide trend assessment was assessed.

reasons: Only one local nest-survey study was assessed; six facets remain not-assessed.
The study estimates one sampled population and is not a systematic review or complete species account.
No independent expert review has been completed.

claims.text: At the Osa Peninsula study sites, vertebrate visits to spider-monkey sleeping-site latrines were recorded by camera traps, and the study reported associations between these sites and higher seedling abundance and dung-beetle biomass than comparison sites.
claims.locator: Abstract; Results §3.2 for camera-trap vertebrate visits; §§3.3–3.4, Fig. 6A and Discussion §4 for dung-beetle and seedling comparisons
claims.placeTimeScope: Osa Peninsula, southwestern Costa Rica; sleeping sites identified in 2017, camera trapping during 2018, and monthly seedling quadrats at focal latrines from August 2018 to April 2019. The results concern sampled sites and measured indicators.
claims.lifeStatus: Free-ranging Ateles geoffroyi and vertebrate visitors at wild forest sites; no captive or domesticated animals are included.

gaps: The study does not establish species-wide effects across the full geographic range, seasons or forest types; causal contribution and long-term population consequences were not assessed.
No phylogenetic or evolutionary evidence was assessed.
A species-wide range inventory and locality history were not assessed; study-site location alone is not a range account.
No fossil evidence or geological age was assessed.
No threat status, trend or range-wide conservation assessment was assessed.

reasons: Only one bounded field ecology study was assessed; six facets remain not-assessed.
The evidence concerns selected Costa Rican study sites and is not a systematic review or complete species account.
No independent expert review has been completed.
